speaker: N
text: A kid stayed awake for eleven days straight, and he did it for a science fair.

speaker: N
text: His name was Randy Gardner, and his friends took shifts keeping him awake.

speaker: N
text: By day two, he couldn't focus his eyes.

speaker: N
text: By day four, he thought a street sign was a person.

speaker: N
text: Then he decided he was a famous football player.

speaker: N
text: But on the last night, he beat a sleep scientist at pinball.

speaker: N
text: So how was his brain still working?

speaker: N
text: You see, scientists think his brain was cheating.

speaker: N
text: It slipped into tiny naps, just seconds long, while his eyes stayed open.

speaker: N
text: They're called microsleeps, and you've probably had one in class.

speaker: N
text: After eleven days, Randy slept fourteen hours and woke up fine.

speaker: N
text: His record was so risky, Guinness stopped accepting new ones.

speaker: N
text: So no one can officially beat the time...
